claims.exact_statement: Van der Steen, Gralka, and Mulla report that asynchronously timed replicating phage populations can permit sequential bacterial resistance acquisition, and report experimental comparison of phage pairs with different collapse-time differences in E. coli MG1655 using p17, p33, and p61.
assumptions: scope limited to the article's in-vitro model and assay
claims.novelty_boundary: not a C13 discovery; timing and order effects are also studied by Wright et al. 2019, https://doi.org/10.1128/mBio.01652-19
claims.costs: Paper reports growth-curve and checkerboard assay designs; actual raw data and supplement were not obtained here. Clinical pharmacokinetics are explicitly not quantified by the article.
claims.falsifier: Not independently reconstructed or tested in this checkpoint.
claims.next_gate: Do not promote as a new mechanism; retain only as prior/source context.

claims.exact_statement: Wu et al. report receptor-dependent phage cross-resistance and sequential acquisition in Salmonella, including LPS-associated mutations before later btuB mutations under a three-phage combination; the article text reports complete resistance by day 6.
assumptions: scope limited to tested Salmonella strain, phages, and in-vitro exposure
claims.novelty_boundary: Supports measuring genotype/resistance-state topology; does not establish a C13 trap or policy.
claims.costs: Article reports WGS for 59 resistant isolates plus cross-resistance and fitness assays; complete mutation transition frequencies and a joint route-risk model were not reconstructed.
claims.falsifier: A reconstructed source table or route analysis showing missing/alternative routes would refine this source-scope summary; no independent audit run.
claims.next_gate: Reconstruct published receptor/genotype/fitness matrices and determine whether transition rates are identifiable.

claims.exact_statement: Muzafar et al. report that E. coli competition changes Salmonella resistance evolution under sub-MIC streptomycin, with aadA-associated effects and context-dependent epistasis in tested resistant isolates.
assumptions: scope limited to the tested synthetic community and exposure
claims.novelty_boundary: Ecological context changing genotype-fitness effects is preexisting source evidence; no general evolutionary trap or controller follows.
claims.costs: Study reports approximately 640 generations and isolate-level assays; no dynamic control or route-level mutation kernel reconstructed.
claims.next_gate: Check whether this fitness evidence can be aligned with the receptor-state data; if not, return UNKNOWN.

claims.exact_statement: A potentially actionable open problem is whether a finite genotype-by-ecological-context transition model, with measured transition supply and context-specific competition/fitness, can improve held-out escape-route prediction or policy selection over equally informed static susceptibility and fitness summaries at matched acquisition cost.
assumptions: transition and observation models acquired rather than assumed
all relevant ecological/phage context measured or explicitly bounded

claims.costs: Requires genotype-linked transition acquisition, sequencing/isolation and fitness measurements across contexts, phage/ecological state tracking, detection calibration, replication, culture time, and compute for uncertainty propagation; unpriced.
claims.falsifier: No held-out prediction/policy benefit over equally informed baselines, omitted escape path, or intervention failing under matched acquisition/exposure costs.
claims.next_gate: Reconstruct data alignment and attempt a finite counterexample or explicit policy attack before asserting capability.
